transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I came in because I’ve taken on way too much lately—more projects, workshops, studio changes, and client calls than I can realistically keep up with. At first it felt productive, but now the deadlines are piling up, and with the mortgage too, it’s starting to feel like it’s closing in on me.
Did these feelings start after you took on the extra projects and financial pressure?
Yes. It’s been going on about three months now, really since I took on the mortgage for the cottage-studio. That’s when it started to feel like the pressure picked up.
Have you been feeling down or depressed?
I’m not really sure I’d call it depressed. I’ve been stressed and weighed down by everything, but I haven’t been noticing a low mood in that way.
Is this stress making it hard for you to function day to day?

Yes, it is. My illustration deadlines have started slipping, and a couple of colleagues have had to check in on me because I’m not keeping up like I usually do. And financially… the mortgage is at risk now because I overcommitted and spent money I really needed to keep the studio secure.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about many different things, even beyond the projects and mortgage?
I’m not sure. Mostly it feels tied to the projects and the mortgage. I don’t think I’m worrying about everything across the board, at least not that I’ve noticed.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?
I don’t know that I’ve lost interest exactly. I’m still drawn to the things I usually like, but I’ve been distracted and under pressure, so I’m not enjoying them as much in the moment.
If the project and mortgage pressure were resolved, do you think these feelings would mostly go away?
I think a lot of it probably would ease up, yes. I can’t say it would all just disappear, but those are the main things weighing on me right now.
Do you feel your distress has been stronger than you would normally expect for these work and mortgage pressures?

I’m not really sure. It feels stressful, but those are big pressures, so I don’t know if my reaction is beyond what would be expected. It’s been bothering me, but I haven’t really measured it against what’s “normal.”
During this period, have you been feeling sad or low most days?
I’m not sure I’d call it sad most days. I’ve had low moments, but it feels more like stress and being worn down than being sad all the time.
Do you find it hard to control the worrying once it starts?
I’m not sure. Sometimes it keeps going in my head for a while, but I don’t know if I’d say I can’t control it. It depends on the day.
Outside of the mortgage and work projects, do you worry a lot about other parts of your life?
Not really, no. I mean, I might think about normal things here and there, but the mortgage and work stuff are the main things on my mind. I haven’t noticed myself worrying a lot about other areas.
Have you gone through a separation or divorce recently?
No, I haven’t gone through a separation or divorce recently.
Have you been feeling hopeless?
I don’t think so. I’ve had some stress, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been feeling hopeless.
Have you been feeling anxious or on edge much of the time?
Not much of the time, no. I get stressed about certain things, but I wouldn’t say I feel anxious or on edge most of the day.
Have you noticed a change in your sleep?
I haven’t really noticed a clear change. My sleep seems about the same, as far as I can tell.
Have you noticed a change in your appetite?
Not really. My appetite seems pretty normal to me—I haven’t noticed any big change.
Have you been feeling tired or low in energy?
I don’t think so. My energy feels pretty normal overall—maybe I get tired like anyone would, but nothing that really stands out.
Would you say this problem is mainly affecting your work?

Yes, mainly work, I think. My illustration deadlines have been slipping, and people I work with have started checking in on me. It’s also gotten into money—I've overcommitted and spent money I needed to keep the studio secure, so now the mortgage is at risk.
Do you feel your reaction to the work and mortgage pressure has been stronger than most people would have in the same situation?
I’m not really sure. I mean, it feels like a lot to me because work and the mortgage are serious, but I don’t know how most people would react in the same situation.
Do you feel your stress has been out of proportion to the work and mortgage problems you’ve been dealing with?
I’m not sure, honestly. It feels like a lot because those are real problems, but I can’t really tell if my stress is beyond what would make sense.
